dimensions.assessment: Affects individuals in the District of Columbia subject to criminal records, youth sentencing under age 18, and drivers subject to traffic enforcement.
dimensions.evidence: This bill repeals District of Columbia (DC) laws related to sealing and expunging criminal records, sentencing of individuals under age 18, and traffic enforcement measures.

dimensions.assessment: Reinstates mandatory minimum sentences and life imprisonment without parole for certain individuals, creating life-changing effects for affected defendants.
dimensions.evidence: reinstates mandatory minimum sentences and life imprisonment (without the possibility of parole or release) for individuals under age 18 at the time an offense was committed.

dimensions.assessment: Eliminates automated traffic enforcement systems and fine liabilities, which has local fiscal effects, but states no specific federal spending amounts.
Amends or repeals multiple District of Columbia statutes relating to traffic cameras, right turns at red lights, criminal record expungement, and juvenile sentencing.
dimensions.evidence: This bill repeals District of Columbia (DC) laws related to sealing and expunging criminal records, sentencing of individuals under age 18, and traffic enforcement measures.

dimensions.assessment: Permanently repeals specified DC laws for future criminal conduct and traffic rules.
dimensions.evidence: shall apply with respect to criminal conduct that occurred after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Specific federal fiscal estimates or budget impact data.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill repeals certain District of Columbia laws regarding criminal record sealing, youth sentencing, and automated traffic enforcement systems, introducing moderate changes to local legal and enforcement procedures.
